extracted.intended_audience: local government communications professionals, municipal managers, and public-sector communicators
extracted.subtask_description: Practical standards and best practices for managing social media and online communications in local government, including community engagement, employee training, moderation, platform use, AI adoption, and measuring campaign impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanize local government leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of humanizing local government leaders and being "human-centered" in communications so public servants and communities best interact with one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make messaging personable and relatable; example: Wigan Council emphasizes being “human-centered.” Use resident voices and authentic storytelling (e.g., co-produced campaigns) to build connection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency when communicating with the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Remain transparent in public communications to build and maintain trust between governing bodies and the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open about decisions and processes; consistent, clear explanations reinforce trust. Avoid opaque language or withholding key information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent messaging across social channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Remain consistent in messaging across social channels to reinforce trust between the governing body and the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate posts and responses so facts and tone do not conflict between platforms or accounts; standardize messages for cross-posting or when correcting misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate in digestible, quick ways
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on communicating in digestible and quick ways while earning the public’s trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer short, plain-language posts tailored to platform norms; prioritize clarity and speed for time-sensitive information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be proactive and innovative in online engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Take a proactive approach to online engagement, maintaining a constant state of innovation and creativity to discover how best to engage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up internal working groups and encourage pilots and experiments to try new formats and platforms; stay alert for new trends and channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be selective and cautious about engagement styles
rubrics_metrics.description: Remain selective when deciding how to engage online, being cautious of unproductive communication styles that could worsen situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize channels and interactions that serve community needs; avoid engagement patterns that escalate conflict or spread misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage trolling and negative comments effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Effectively manage online trolling and negative comments directed at a municipality or its staff; adopt approaches like “take the cue not the bait.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance listening for legitimate concerns with avoiding amplifying antagonistic content. Don't reflexively escalate; assess whether a response helps or harms the conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance listening with avoiding escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: Listen to community input and identify needs visible through negative commentary while being cautious about worsening the situation through unproductive responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat negative comments as potential signals for service issues or misinformation, but avoid reactive or inflammatory replies that could escalate trolling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize messaging when correcting misinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Work alongside law enforcement and adjacent councils to standardize messaging when correcting misinformation, ensuring consistency and helping to build public trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate across agencies to present a unified correction; use agreed-upon language and avoid contradictory statements that undermine credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. comment moderation approach respecting free speech
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that deleting negative comments may raise First Amendment concerns; instead build parameters that honor citizens’ right to free speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wentzville’s three principles: (1) Respond to the question directly; (2) Correct the misinformation; (3) Provide contact information to direct the person’s question or comment to the proper resource. Use these as a moderation workflow rather than blanket removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish Communication Ambassador groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Create stakeholder groups (business owners, HOA trustees, residents) who act as advocates and help bridge gaps between employees and residents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage ambassadors to share accurate information, amplify official messages, and mitigate misinformation; recruit diverse stakeholders to reflect community makeup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform-specific strategies and audience analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Use different social media platforms for different purposes; analyze audiences and social media trends to decide which platform to use when.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map message types to platform strengths (e.g., visual content on Instagram/TikTok, long-form on YouTube, neighborhood discussion on Nextdoor). Regularly assess audience demographics and platform trends to allocate resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Play to the channel — layered communications strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement layered communications that run in parallel to social media (e-newsletters, phone/text alerts) and understand what it takes to make the most impact on each channel—"playing to whatever the channel wants."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine push (alerts, emails) and pull (social posts) tactics; tailor format, tone, and timing to each channel’s conventions for maximum reach and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot new ideas and monitor platform adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Be willing to try new ideas and pilot programs as platforms evolve, balancing experimentation with monitoring which platforms gain traction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run small pilots, measure engagement and outcomes, then scale successful approaches. Avoid committing large resources to unproven platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require social media training during onboarding
rubrics_metrics.description: Require social media training as part of employee onboarding so staff are equipped to spread accurate information while complying with policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide role-specific training, refreshers, and clear policy documents; ensure employees understand boundaries and escalation paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uphold apolitical policies and codes of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure employees understand and comply with policies relating to the apolitical nature of council work (especially during election periods); use integrity commissioners and reporting mechanisms as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify acceptable personal vs. official use of social media and provide avenues to report violations; include election-period guidance and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguard employee well-being and watch for stress
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize staff well-being by watching for signs of stress and protecting employees who may become targets online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor workloads, provide mental-health resources, apply moderation policies that reduce direct harassment of staff, and intervene when staff safety is threatened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach AI as a complementary tool with ethical safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat AI as an opportunity to complement council work while remaining cautious of ethical and risk considerations; provide training and policy for AI use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AI for time-saving tasks and productivity gains but train staff on responsible use, maintain oversight, and adopt the posture of “be on the cutting edge but not the bleeding edge.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-produce campaigns with residents
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage residents in co-producing campaigns (e.g., LINA domestic violence campaign) to create personable, moving, and effective content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Involve volunteer residents in design and messaging; leverage lived experience for authenticity, and use in-house marketing/design resources to amplify resident-led content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure campaign outcomes and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Track measurable outcomes from social media campaigns (e.g., increases in hotline calls, recruitment responses) to demonstrate effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define KPIs up front (calls, applications, engagement metrics), collect baseline data, and report outcomes (example: 72% increase in calls after campaign). Use results to iterate on strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use creative, targeted recruitment strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Use engaging and 'fun' social media recruitment and advertising methods targeted to specific audiences (e.g., youth) to meet hiring needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design platform-appropriate recruitment content, target demographics, and measure hires attributable to campaigns; innovate in outreach to solve local labor shortages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage internal PR teams and dedicated working groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the creativity and innovation of internal public relations teams alongside specific working groups focused on developing engaging content and staying alert about new developments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form cross-functional teams to maintain creativity and consistency; assign responsibility for trend-spotting, content creation, and community engagement strategies.
